UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (articles 25-37 on SL formation and registered office); Real Decreto 165/2019, de 22 de marzo, and Law 5/2018, de 17 de abril, establishing the Registro de Titulares Reales; Order JUS/268/2019, de 5 de marzo, on the UBO electronic register; Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive 2018/843 (5AMLD) transposition.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Accepted for the SL's administrative correspondence and management address, provided a physical Spanish registered office exists (an SL must maintain a real address in Spain for notification and legal representation). A pure virtual mailbox without personnel or access to accounting records is not sufficient for the AML/tax registered-office test; however, a serviced office, co-working suite or company-administrated address is accepted by the Mercantile Registry and AEAT when all statutory records are actually available there.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (certificación negativa de denominación); Registro Mercantil Provincial del domicilio social (inscripción registral); intervención obligatoria de Notario; notificación electrónica al BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil).

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Art. 4 (capital mínimo de EUR 3,000 para la SL), Arts. 20 a 22 (escritura pública e inscripción en el Registro Mercantil), Art. 22 bis (constitución telemática), Art. 23 (contenido de la escritura), Arts. 33 y 34 (personalidad jurídica y sociedad en formación), Art. 60 (desembolso del capital); Reglamento del Registro Mercantil aprobado por Real Decreto 1784/1996.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución otorgada ante notario español e inscripción de la sociedad en la hoja registral (inscripción 1ª) del Registro Mercantil Provincial competente.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 101 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Capital social mínimo obligatorio de EUR 3,000, íntegramente suscrito y desembolsado en efectivo antes del otorgamiento de la escritura (LSC Arts. 4, 16 y 60). El desembolso debe acreditarse mediante certificado bancario de depósito en una entidad de crédito española a nombre de la sociedad en constitución. Los socios no residentes pueden ostentar el 100% del capital y realizar el depósito transfiriendo fondos a la cuenta provisional. Existe el régimen excepcional de sociedad limitada de formación sucesiva (Art. 4.2 LSC) que admite capital inicial inferior, con restricciones de reparto y obligación de completar los EUR 3,000 con beneficios; en la práctica, una sociedad exportadora mayorista suscribe EUR 3,000 en efectivo.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate (Certificado del instalador autorizado in accordance with R.D. 2267/2004 Reglamento de Seguridad contra Incendios) certifying the installation of portable extinguishers at a maximum coverage of 200 m² each, emergency lighting, signage, and evacuation routes; structural load certificate for the pallet racking system; occupational risk prevention program under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales including a written risk assessment, emergency and evacuation plan, and the engagement of a certified external prevention service; labor inspectorate clearance may be required before the commencement of operations when the workforce equals or exceeds six employees.

Paid-in capital rule: Capital social mínimo obligatorio de EUR 3,000, íntegramente suscrito y desembolsado en efectivo antes del otorgamiento de la escritura (LSC Arts. 4, 16 y 60). El desembolso debe acreditarse mediante certificado bancario de depósito en una entidad de crédito española a nombre de la sociedad en constitución. Los socios no residentes pueden ostentar el 100% del capital y realizar el depósito transfiriendo fondos a la cuenta provisional. Existe el régimen excepcional de sociedad limitada de formación sucesiva (Art. 4.2 LSC) que admite capital inicial inferior, con restricciones de reparto y obligación de completar los EUR 3,000 con beneficios; en la práctica, una sociedad exportadora mayorista suscribe EUR 3,000 en efectivo.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The founding shareholders, having subscribed the full share capital of EUR 3,000 deposited in the corporate escrow account, approve: (1) adoption of the corporate name and establishment of the registered office; (2) appointment of the Sole Administrator, granting the broadest powers to execute all incorporation and licensing formalities before the Mercantile Registry, Tax Agency, Customs and municipal authorities; (3) ratification of all actions performed in the name of the company prior to registration; (4) opening of bank accounts in Spain; (5) filing of provisional and definitive tax identification applications; and (6) initiation of the municipal opening license, sanitary registration (RGSEAA), and excise warehouse procedures.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Consejería de Industria de la Comunidad Autónoma and Ayuntamiento del municipio through the Ventanilla Única Empresa (VUE); technical verifications by authorized industrial technicians

Category: Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento de Actividad Económica (or Comunicación Ambiental Previa / Declaración Responsable, depending on the municipal ordinance and the size of the warehouse)

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

A Spanish SL is formed by notarial deed and registration in the Mercantile Registry. The SL must then submit Form 036/037 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) to obtain or confirm its definitive NIF and VAT registration. A foreign non-resident entity acting without a Spanish SL but through a permanent establishment must request a non-resident NIF through Form 036/037 using a tax representative, filing a notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation, proof of representative authority, and evidence of the Spanish permanent establishment registration. For intra-Community supplies and purchases, the taxpayer must be assigned a NIF-IVA, which is applied for through the same census declaration and must be reflected in VIES records.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation (a Spanish SL is a capital entity taxed under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades at the standard 25% rate; it is resident and taxed on worldwide income. Territorial rules apply only to non-resident entities without a permanent establishment, and Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment is limited to qualifying entities in the Canary Islands ZEC regime.) — A Spanish SL is formed by notarial deed and registration in the Mercantile Registry. The SL must then submit Form 036/037 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) to obtain or confirm its definitive NIF and VAT registration. A foreign non-resident entity acting without a Spanish SL but through a permanent establishment must request a non-resident NIF through Form 036/037 using a tax representative, filing a notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation, proof of representative authority, and evidence of the Spanish permanent establishment registration. For intra-Community supplies and purchases, the taxpayer must be assigned a NIF-IVA, which is applied for through the same census declaration and must be reflected in VIES records.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation (a Spanish SL is a capital entity taxed under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades at the standard 25% rate; it is resident and taxed on worldwide income. Territorial rules apply only to non-resident entities without a permanent establishment, and Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment is limited to qualifying entities in the Canary Islands ZEC regime.)

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections include the group tax consolidation regime for Spanish-based groups with at least 75% direct or indirect voting control, the VAT group (Grupo IVA) regime, options on depreciation and asset amortisation methods, and the simplified VAT regime for small business where turnover and purchases are each below EUR 250,000. Hybrid mismatch rules implementing ATAD apply and prevent elective arbitrage through dual classification.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

There is no general turnover threshold for ordinary VAT registration: any legal person performing taxable economic activity in Spain must register before commencing activity. The simplified IVA regime is available only to small traders with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 250,000 and annual purchases not exceeding EUR 250,000; a wholesale spirits-export trader exceeding those limits, or opting out, must operate under the general IVA regime.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods consigned to a destination outside the EU are exempt with right to a zero rate under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law; the exporter must prove that the goods physically left the territory of the European Union within the statutory period and hold transport, customs, and commercial evidence. For a Chinese baijiu wholesale export operation to Latin America through a Spanish SL, zero-rating requires a valid customs export declaration (DUA) and proof of international freight. Intra-Community dispatches to EU customers may likewise be zero-rated if the customer is VIES-registered and the goods are transported to another Member State; EC sales list reporting is mandatory.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) with customs documentary
  • Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment to the third-country destination
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT wire/letter-of-credit collection evidence showing receipt of payment from the foreign buyer
  • Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin
  • CMR or alternative transport document for intra-Community dispatches where applicable
  • e-AD (electronic administrative document) proving excise duty suspension or export release for ethyl alcohol
  • VAT refund file or formal declaration supporting the zero-rated nature of the supply

Spain mandates electronic invoicing for B2B transactions under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and RD 1007/2023. The mandate is phased by turnover: enterprises with annual turnover above EUR 8 million are required in the first phase, all remaining operators in the subsequent phase. Invoicing must be exchanged using a certified electronic invoicing solution guaranteeing authenticity and integrity, commonly in Facturae XML format. Billing software must comply with AEAT 'Verifactu' technical requirements. Large businesses with turnover above EUR 6,010,121.42, or those included in an SII VAT group, must transmit invoice records to AEAT in near real-time under the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) using web-service APIs, generally within 8 calendar days for paper documents and 4 calendar days for fully electronic records.

If AEAT determines that the export zero-rating claim was not substantiated, false, or the goods did not depart the EU, the exporter is assessed Spanish VAT at the standard rate of 21% on the invoiced value plus late-payment interest. Tax penalties under Ley General Tributaria articles 191 and 193 range from 50% to 150% of the tax amount involved, with the 150% penalty applicable in cases of concealment or repeated irregular practice. Criminal liability under Article 305 of the Criminal Code may be pursued where defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, exposing corporate representatives to imprisonment and fines. AEAT may retrospectively claw back refunds or VAT credits for up to four years and impose additional excise duty and transfer-pricing penalties when alcohol export or customs evidence is defective.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

The euro is fully convertible across current and capital accounts, with Spain applying the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Articles 63-65 on free movement of capital. There are no convertibility restrictions on current-account transactions, trade settlements, or profit remittances. Non-resident profit repatriation is lawful but technically subject to domestic withholding tax (typically 19% on dividends, reduced by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or the applicable double tax treaty) and requires evidenciary support of distributable reserves prepared under Spanish GAAP. Capital-account movements are liberalized; however, statistical declarations to the Bank of Spain and the DGCIIN are mandatory for foreign direct investments exceeding EUR 3,000,000 (form D1A/D2A), while lower-value investments and settlements above EUR 50,000 per month must be notified through the bank in the monthly balance-of-payments reporting cycle under Law 19/1993 and Banco de España Circular 1/2011, as amended by Circular 1/2020. The equity injection for the SL falls within a liberalized regime, subject to post-event filing rather than prior administrative authorization, unless the investment triggers sector-specific screening under Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 (e.g., critical infrastructures, dual-use, security, media), which does not apply to an alcoholic beverage wholesaler.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds and no required conversion ratio. Eurozone residents may freely retain foreign currency receipts in domestic or offshore accounts. Nevertheless, all export collections must be traceable and supported by customs declarations (Export Control System of the AEAT, with TARIC nomenclature) and commercial invoices. For each transaction or monthly aggregation exceeding EUR 50,000, the settlement must be included in the bank's statistical report to the Bank of Spain. Exporters must retain documentary proof of receipt (SWIFT MT103 advice, bill of lading, customs release) for at least five years to satisfy tax and anti-money-laundering audit requirements.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is the Spanish central bank and primary banking supervisor; the European Central Bank (ECB) anchors the Eurosystem monetary framework, TARGET2 real-time gross settlement, and single supervisory mechanism for significant credit institutions. The Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN), part of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, administers Spain's foreign investment registry and statistical declaration regime.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Low-Medium with significant legal constraints. A non-EEA digital e-money institution (e.g., UK-licensed EMIs, Singapore or Hong Kong neobanks) cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a Spanish SL without obtaining authorization as an Entidad de Dinero Electrónico from Banco de España or passporting an existing EEA license under Directive 2009/110/EC and PSD2. Offshore EMIs lacking a local EUR IBAN and an FGD (Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund) membership create operational fragility for LC-based trade flows, daily sweeps, and excise duty payments. A domestic Tier-1 bank with UCP600 documentary credit capability is the only recommended primary treasury vehicle. An EEA-passported EMI (e.g., Irish or Lithuanian licensed emitters) may be used solely for small-ticket operating expenses, but should not hold the capital escrow or process supplier settlements above EUR 50,000 due to counterparty risk and the absence of trade finance products.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Ultimate beneficial ownership traceable to the People's Republic of China triggers mandatory enhanced due diligence under EU Directive 2015/849 and Spanish Law 10/2010, especially when the PRC shareholder exhibits a complex group structure or residential address inconsistencies.

Root cause: Ultimate beneficial ownership traceable to the People's Republic of China triggers mandatory enhanced due diligence under EU Directive 2015/849 and Spanish Law 10/2010, especially when the PRC shareholder exhibits a complex group structure or residential address inconsistencies.

Defense evidence: A notarized and apostilled UBO declaration (Registro de Titularidades Reales), three years of audited financial statements of each 25%-plus shareholder, a criminal record certificate for each UBO, bank references from a Tier-1 Chinese bank, a legal entity structure chart with percentage interests, and an affidavit accounting for the source of funds used for the capital injection.
High-proof baijiu classified as alcohol subject to excise duty (Ley 12/2013 and Directive 2020/262) activates sector risk flags, particularly when tax warehouse receipts or Spanish import/export authorizations are missing, or when shipments appear routed to jurisdictions with weak controls.

Root cause: High-proof baijiu classified as alcohol subject to excise duty (Ley 12/2013 and Directive 2020/262) activates sector risk flags, particularly when tax warehouse receipts or Spanish import/export authorizations are missing, or when shipments appear routed to jurisdictions with weak controls.

Defense evidence: The AEAT-issued excise import/export authorization, the EU excise movement (e-AD) records, all customs entry summaries and export declarations, certificates of origin (Form A or EUR.1), warehouse receipts from the Spanish bonded warehouse operator, and the complete chain of commercial contracts from the China producer to the Spanish SL and onward to the Latin America buyer.
High-frequency cross-border wires in USD/CNH with mismatched trade purpose codes are tagged as 'pass-through' or trade-based money-laundering red flags, particularly when invoice value diverges from market benchmarks for distilled spirits.

Root cause: High-frequency cross-border wires in USD/CNH with mismatched trade purpose codes are tagged as 'pass-through' or trade-based money-laundering red flags, particularly when invoice value diverges from market benchmarks for distilled spirits.

Defense evidence: The full shipment document set (bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, insurance certificate), an explicit MT103 purpose-code matrix pre-approved by the bank's compliance desk, a quarterly trade forecast, pricing benchmarks from recognized spirits market indices, and copies of all UCP600 documentary presentations for LC disbursements.
Directors or signatories without a substantial physical footprint in Spain are flagged as 'ghost directors,' especially when the registered office is a virtual mailbox rather than a genuine commercial premise.

Root cause: Directors or signatories without a substantial physical footprint in Spain are flagged as 'ghost directors,' especially when the registered office is a virtual mailbox rather than a genuine commercial premise.

Defense evidence: A Registro Mercantil certificate of incumbency, a genuine Spanish lease agreement for the SL's registered office, the directors' NIE certificates, a Spanish payroll or social security filing demonstrating local substance, and an apostilled board resolution appointing the bank signing authority.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

The shareholder's capital contribution must be initiated as a SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's EUR-denominated IBAN. The wire must reference the Banco de España statistical purpose code for foreign direct investment in equity (code 3001-3002, 'Inversión directa — capital social'), and the beneficiary bank will require a covering memorandum stating 'Apoyo de capital social' and the notarized capital increase resolution. For injections exceeding EUR 3,000,000, the SL must file a post-investment declaration (Modelo D1A) with the Ministry of Economy's Foreign Investment Register within 30 days of the settlement; smaller injections are reported statistically through the bank, monthly. Foreign-currency wires (USD or CNH) must be converted to EUR at the bank's best-execution rate under MiFID II; TARGET2 settlement is used for the final EUR credit. The bank will withhold crediting until the KYC pack, including the RENACEO (Registro de Titularidades Reales) confirmation and the SL's deed of incorporation, is cleared.Outbound payments include (1) sight/fixed-date SWIFT MT103 for urgent supplier advances and small-value purchases; (2) MT102 for batch supplier settlements within SEPA; and (3) documentary trade settlement via SWIFT MT700 Series (advising, confirmation, amendment) strictly under UCP600, with the Spanish bank confirming the LC for the benefit of the Chinese exporter. The recommended clearing structure for high-value baijiu exports into Latin America is a confirmed irrevocable LC drawn at sight, requiring presentation of a full set of bills of lading, phytosanitary and alcohol content certificates, and the customs export declaration (DEX). Same-day EUR clearing within the EU operates via SEPA Credit Transfer Instant (SCT Inst) with a 10-second cap, while urgent extra-EUR finality is assured by TARGET2 RTGS. For USD settlement, the Spanish bank routes through its US correspondent (e.g., via the Federal Reserve wire network) with a corresponding MT202 cover instruction.Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH) with tenors up to 24 months, entered under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Spanish bank or EEA-passported bank, subject to EMIR margin obligations, and used to fix export proceeds conversion.Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNH/CNY, lawfully executed by a Spanish authorized credit institution or an EEA-passported broker and settled in EUR/USD offshore, provided no CNY delivery occurs within Spain; the bank will hedge back-to-back on the international CNH desk.Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) converting USD or CNH trade inflows into EUR for the SL's bond and supplier payment profile, subject to EMIR trade reporting and clearing thresholds.FX zero-premium collars and participating forwards for the USD leg, permissible for corporates classified as 'eligible counterparties' or 'professional clients' under MiFID II, recommended when annual notional exposure exceeds EUR 5,000,000.Natural hedging within a multi-currency current account (EUR/USD/CNH balances) is permissible without a separate derivative product, but must be reflected at fair value in the SL's year-end Spanish GAAP financial statements.EURIBOR-based interest-rate swaps to hedge floating-rate pre-export financing and trade-loan exposure, permissible only when the swap is transacted with the relationship lending bank and documented under the same ISDA schedule.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium with significant legal constraints. A non-EEA digital e-money institution (e.g., UK-licensed EMIs, Singapore or Hong Kong neobanks) cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a Spanish SL without obtaining authorization as an Entidad de Dinero Electrónico from Banco de España or passporting an existing EEA license under Directive 2009/110/EC and PSD2. Offshore EMIs lacking a local EUR IBAN and an FGD (Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund) membership create operational fragility for LC-based trade flows, daily sweeps, and excise duty payments. A domestic Tier-1 bank with UCP600 documentary credit capability is the only recommended primary treasury vehicle. An EEA-passported EMI (e.g., Irish or Lithuanian licensed emitters) may be used solely for small-ticket operating expenses, but should not hold the capital escrow or process supplier settlements above EUR 50,000 due to counterparty risk and the absence of trade finance products.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities may generally apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions and eligibility conditions.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-resident recipients, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to qualifying EU or European Economic Area corporate recipients, generally requiring at least a 5% direct participation held for at least one year, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions, and beneficial ownership or equivalent anti-conduit requirements.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

The return is generally due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing period is 1 July through 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the deadline is extended under the applicable electronic filing rules.

Deadline: · Frequency:

The normal filing windows are 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October, and 1 to 20 December. Direct debit normally requires an earlier cutoff. The payment calculation may use either the prior-period tax liability basis or the current-period accounting result basis where the statutory conditions and election apply.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally due during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal period is 1 November through 30 November of the following year.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Mandatory documentation is generally triggered where the Spanish taxpayer's aggregate related-party transactions of the same type and under the same valuation method exceed EUR 100,000, or where aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 based on market value during the tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. A master file is generally required for taxpayers forming part of a group, subject to exemptions including the group-size and turnover rules. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a single standalone Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulation regime applicable to every company. Substance is nevertheless material under the General Tax Law anti-abuse rule, beneficial-ownership principles, treaty principal-purpose and anti-conduit concepts, EU anti-tax-avoidance rules, participation-exemption conditions, interest and royalty exemptions, and permanent-establishment analysis. The SL should maintain real decision-making, appropriate personnel, premises or operational capacity, commercial risk control, accounting records, bank activity, inventory and logistics evidence, and arm's-length pricing proportionate to its baijiu export-distribution functions.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate income tax reporting

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on concealment, fraud, and severity. Serious tax fraud involving amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 may constitute a criminal offense, with fines commonly linked to the evaded amount and potential imprisonment of one to five years; aggravated cases may carry higher penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may face joint or subsidiary tax liability, civil restitution, criminal fines, disqualification from management, and imprisonment. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require judicial or enforcement authority; assets may be frozen or seized.
Transfer-pricing manipulation and profit diversion

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may make a primary transfer-pricing adjustment, impose corporate income tax, late-payment interest, and documentation-related penalties. Failure to provide or correctly provide transfer-pricing documentation can produce fixed penalties per missing or incorrect data point and, where tax is affected, proportional penalties linked to the adjustment.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur civil liability for tax damage and, in intentional cases, criminal exposure for tax fraud, accounting falsification, or asset concealment. A group relationship does not automatically protect directors from liability for deliberate misconduct.
False export, customs, VAT, or excise documentation

Statutory sanction: The taxpayer may lose VAT exemption, repay VAT and deductions, and incur VAT, customs, and excise penalties. Goods may be detained or seized, and customs debt, interest, and administrative fines may arise. Repeated or intentional customs fraud may become criminal.

Director personal liability: Responsible directors and customs or tax representatives may face joint liability, civil recovery, seizure of assets, professional disqualification, and criminal prosecution where documents are knowingly falsified. Imprisonment is possible for serious fraud; travel restrictions require a judicial order.
Alcohol regulatory and excise non-compliance

Statutory sanction: Authorities may impose excise assessments, penalties, suspension or withdrawal of authorizations, seizure or destruction of non-compliant goods, and restrictions on commercial activity. Serious smuggling or organized excise fraud may result in criminal prosecution.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for intentional regulatory breaches, unpaid public charges, and damage caused by unsafe or unlawfully marketed products. Criminal sanctions may include fines and imprisonment in serious cases.
Shell company, beneficial ownership, and treaty abuse

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may deny treaty, participation-exemption, interest, or royalty relief, recharacterize transactions, assess withholding and corporate tax, and impose interest and penalties. The tax authority may apply the Spanish anti-abuse rule or the principal-purpose test.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil tax liability, disqualification, asset-preservation measures, and criminal charges where the structure involves fraud, document falsification, or money laundering. Travel bans and imprisonment are possible only under applicable judicial or criminal procedures.
Anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations

Statutory sanction: Spanish AML authorities may impose substantial administrative fines, publicize sanctions, suspend activities, and require enhanced controls. Money laundering may constitute a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment and fines; sanctions breaches may trigger additional administrative or criminal consequences under applicable EU and Spanish measures.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may face personal fines, civil confiscation, asset freezing, management disqualification, and imprisonment. Travel restrictions may be imposed by judicial order or under applicable sanctions measures.
Accounting falsification and concealed distributions

Statutory sanction: Consequences may include tax reassessment, penalties, rejection of deductions, shareholder restitution, insolvency liability, and criminal sanctions for accounting falsification, fraudulent administration, or creditor prejudice.

Director personal liability: Directors may be required to restore assets, compensate the company and creditors, bear subsidiary tax or insolvency liability, and face disqualification or imprisonment where criminal elements are established.
Failure to retain records and respond to AEAT audits

Statutory sanction: Separate accounting, record-keeping, obstruction, and information-reporting penalties may apply in addition to any tax assessment. The authority may use indirect estimation where reliable records are unavailable.

Director personal liability: Directors may face personal penalties for obstruction or deliberate destruction, civil liability for resulting tax loss, and criminal exposure where evidence is concealed or falsified. Imprisonment or travel restrictions require the applicable criminal or judicial process.
